meta.source: Carreno Ruiz & D'Ambrosio, 'Validation of the gamma-Re_theta transition model for airfoils operating in the very low Reynolds number regime', Flow, Turbulence and Combustion 109:279-308 (2022), Fig. 19 (p. 305). File: sa-ai/references/carreno-ruiz2022-gammaRetheta-STARCCM-e387-Re60k.pdf
meta.condition: Eppler 387 airfoil, Re = 60,000. gamma-Re_theta transition model in STAR-CCM+ (2D, incompressible).
meta.legend_note: Fig. 19's legend shows a SINGLE CFD curve labeled only 'gamma-Re_theta' -- unlike Figs. 10-13 of the same paper, this figure does NOT separate Menter vs Suluksna-Juntasaro correlation sets. The text does not state which calibration Fig. 19 uses; from Section 6 context (Fig. 17 caption: 'Suluksna-Juntasaro calibration with the s1 parameter set to 6') it is most plausibly the SJ s1=6 recalibration, and the Conclusions state that this recalibration replicates Menter's calibration closely for performance coefficients. The other legend entries are literature/experiment references: Experimental (McGhee et al. 1988, NASA TM-4062 LTPT), 2D NS (Sahin et al. 2008), 3D DNS (Sahin et al. 2008), 3D LES (Frere et al.).
meta.method: Figure is an embedded raster image (1418x598 px, MATLAB export) -- page.get_drawings() vector extraction not available (only clip rectangles), so the image was extracted at native resolution and digitized by MATLAB-default-color segmentation. Axes calibrated by least-squares on detected gridline pixel positions (residual < 0.5 px). Scatter markers located as bounding-box centers of color-clustered blobs (legend samples excluded by region); the gamma-Re_theta curve sampled at integer alpha via column-median of blue pixels (markers sit at integer alpha).
meta.uncertainty: Born-digital but raster-embedded figure. Calibration residual <0.5 px; marker localization ~1-2 px. Pixel scales: 1 px = 0.021 deg alpha, 0.0026 CL, 0.00021 CD. Estimated 1-sigma digitization uncertainty: alpha +/-0.05 deg, CL +/-0.005, CD +/-0.0005.
meta.alpha_grid_note: All series plotted at integer alpha; alpha snapped to integers (raw centers within 0.05 deg of integers).
